analysis.description: This paper investigates how engaging in resistance-based exercise (calisthenics) in nature-based and indoor settings affects affective valence, perceived exertion, visual attention, movement adaptability, heart rate variability, and performance. The study contributes to understanding the impact of the environment on exercising by conducting a trial with participants randomized into two groups, assessing multiple psychological and physiological aspects.

type.justification: The study conducts a randomized controlled trial, collecting empirical data on the effects of exercise settings on various performance and psychological metrics.
